title: Explicit inverse transitions for the existing negative two-term tensor
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with Grothendieck topology $J$ and commutative ring sheaf $\mathcal O$. Use the negative two-term factors, their ordered tensor and basis of [def-cbc-signed-koszul-completion-model], and the scalar map and total tensor of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. For a global section $b$ and $m\in\mathbf N$, define the factor transition from exponent $m+2$ to $m+1$ to have multiplication by $b$ in degree $-1$, identity in degree zero, and zero elsewhere, with the canonical two-term identifications. Its chain equation is $b b^{m+1}=b^{m+2}$. Define the transition on an ordered tensor recursively by tensoring the first-factor transition with the tail transition. For zero factors the transition is the identity of $\mathcal O[0]$. All these maps are explicit constructions, with no existential choice. For the empty tensor, inverse Hom-unit evaluation is a chain isomorphism to the positive internal dual, and it intertwines the identity transitions and the empty-subset degree-zero unit.
